# Enhance existing articles before creating new ones

Make your best page more useful before you write a rival to it. This guide helps you choose where new facts and stories belong. Start with a search of your site and the page list you keep.

**The path:** New material → Existing-page search → Improve, support or create decision → Reviewed draft

**Start when:** New material or a content request may overlap a topic the site already covers.

## Inputs

- [Inventory pages and their purpose](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page#task-step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page) and [Map actual content roles](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves#task-map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves) with current topic owners and source revisions.
- The actual new recording, facts, proof or reader question, plus use permissions and [Goals, Content, Targeting: the result, source material and people served](https://blitzmetrics.com/gct-business-strategy/).
- Current page owner, maintained source/builder and the authority for any edit, consolidation or publication.

## Steps

1. Search the maintained inventory, site search and relevant query variants before choosing a new URL. Inspect the actual pages that address the reader’s question. Search results can miss pages; combine them with the source inventory and record any scope limits.
2. Compare the new material with each candidate’s reader, promise, method and proof. Choose the page that owns the same intent, not just the page with a matching keyword. A task recipe, a topic hub, a service offer and a distinct case story can legitimately discuss the same subject.
3. If an owning page exists, prepare a specific enhancement: a clearer definition, corrected method, new source-backed example, current fact or useful visual. Retain relevant proof, author voice, existing media and stable URL/type. Explain what the reader can do better after the change.
4. If the material is a distinct execution, event or case, give it its own supporting story when useful and link it to the owning method. Do not paste a second generic explanation into a competing hub. If no page serves a genuinely distinct core topic, propose a new hub or task recipe with the proper role.
5. When coverage is fragmented, inventory unique value before proposing consolidation. Use [Review duplicate or weak pages](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=remove-duplicate-thin-pages#task-remove-duplicate-thin-pages) for the exact keep/merge/remove decision and destination checks. Two pages that mention the same topic are not automatically duplicates, and a merge proposal is not permission to delete or redirect.
6. Apply [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/) to the proposed page: grade-five opening, clear reader value, useful first-screen visual and evidence-backed claims. Keep relevant named proof and strongest credible sources visible; an attractive rewrite that loses real examples has not improved the page.
7. Save the enhance/support/create decision, exact source diff and receiving owner. Favor proven useful material when allocating work, but use the source’s Greatest Hits ratio as a planning principle, not a fixed performance law or a ban on fresh evidence. Publish only through the actual authorized rail and verify the result.

## Definition of done (QA checklist)

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] The decision compares actual intent and evidence, with one maintained owner for the same topic.
- [ ] Distinct task recipes, offers and real supporting stories are not erased just for sharing terms.
- [ ] The proposed improvement preserves unique facts, media and voice and meets current reading and visual standards.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

## Example(s)

**Fictional teaching example. This is not a client result or proof of a completed run.**

A fictional plumber has a drain-cleaning guide and a new filmed repair. The film adds a useful diagnostic detail, so the team improves that section. The unusual repair also supports a separate dated case story linked to the guide and the real service page. It does not create a second drain-cleaning guide or invent a sales result.

[Create or update the owning recipe](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=create-or-update-a-definitive-article#task-create-or-update-a-definitive-article) receives an accepted recipe change; [Place the accepted links](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-4-create-links-with-proper-anchor-text-and-placement#task-step-4-create-links-with-proper-anchor-text-and-placement) receives its link plan. The content inventory records the decision and the exact next owner.

This task supports the [Content Factory: Produce, Process, Post and Promote](https://blitzmetrics.com/content-factory/). Identity, proof, access or coordination can support several stages. Use the real inputs and receiving owner above; this task does not create unrelated transcripts, clips or ads merely because the diagram has four stages.

Give the [AI worker](https://blitzmetrics.com/build-agents/) this recipe, the real inputs, desired result and actions already authorized. Ask for the saved output, sources, checks and next owner. A [skill is a written recipe](https://localservicespotlight.com/plugin/); loading one does not prove account access or perform the task. Use the [installation guide](https://localservicespotlight.com/install/) if reusable setup is needed. A ZIP is a source snapshot, not an access grant or automatic update.

Use the app’s actual supported tools and verified file/account access. Keep a missing human verification step with its real owner. Recurring work needs its own configured job, trigger, timezone and observed result; this guide creates no schedule. Before any media playback, mute the player and set its volume to zero. If silence cannot be verified first, use captions, frames, metadata or another silent check.

## Record the real execution

Open the run record when work begins. Keep one execution ID, starting recipe revision, real inputs and current state. ## Steps

1. State the reader’s task or question and the evidence this piece supplies. Compare that purpose with the current map before choosing a URL. A generic subject label such as “marketing” does not tell you whether the piece is a recipe, a topic explanation or a dated story.

# Follow entity linking decision tree

Help readers reach the right person, business or guide. This task checks what each name means and where its link should go. Start with the draft and a list of the names and ideas it uses.

**The path:** Named subject → Identity and page-role check → Useful destination → In-context review

## Inputs

- The [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/) method and necessary direct source, sign-in, install or download destinations used by the task.

## Steps

1. Read the actual sentences and list the names and unfamiliar terms they contain. Record whether each item means a person, an organization, a method, a tool or a particular piece of evidence. Resolve ambiguous names before linking; a matching title in search is not identity proof.
2. Route a person to their verified personal home and an in-network business to its verified official site. Check that the page describes the same entity and current relationship. Do not use a look-alike name, obsolete affiliate destination or unrelated profile merely because it opens.
3. For a BlitzMetrics method, choose the maintained owned explanation. For an outside tool, concept or well-known entity in explanatory copy, use our current guide when one exists. 4. Keep direct primary evidence and required action links when the step needs that destination. Label a research source, account sign-in or download by its real purpose; these are different from the first explanation of the tool. Do not retarget a source citation or login button to our general article.
5. Explain unfamiliar language on its first useful body mention in plain words, linked to the owned guide. Keep headings short and meaningful; if the term first occurs in a heading, give its explanation in the next suitable prose. Do not expand every repeated mention or repeatedly link the same entity.
6. Use the actual name or a concise phrase that predicts the destination. Three to six descriptive words is the house preference where natural, not a requirement to pad a two-word person’s name. Read the surrounding sentence after the edit to ensure the meaning and claim remain true.

# Identify and eliminate orphan/standalone articles

Help readers find useful pages that your site has left out. This guide checks pages with no link leading to them and plans the right fix. Start with the full page list, then compare it with the links people can follow.

**The path:** All published URLs → Incoming-path check → Keep, connect or review → Fresh crawl

## Inputs

- [Map actual content roles](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves#task-map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves) with actual page roles, parents, incoming body links and site navigation.
- Current content sources and valuable facts/media, search data if available, and authority for exact edits or removals.

## Steps

1. Reconcile the published CMS list, sitemap and crawl before flagging orphans. A crawler that follows only existing links can miss the very pages being sought. Record excluded content types, private pages and failed fetches, and keep inaccessible records unknown rather than treating them as zero-link pages.
2. For each published URL, distinguish incoming internal links, outgoing links and a mapped parent. A page with no detected incoming path is an orphan candidate within the measured scope even if its category or parent is known. Check both body links and usable navigation, recording which definition the count uses.
3. Read each candidate for reader purpose, unique evidence, business function and current relevance. Choose connect, improve, consolidate-review, remove-review or intentionally unlisted with a reason. Utility or campaign pages may have a valid limited role; absence from the main topic tree alone is not permission to delete them.
4. For a useful content page, add a natural incoming link from its relevant existing hub or other suitable page, with a short explanation of its value. Add the page’s own parent or service link where useful. An outgoing link from the orphan does not itself create an incoming route.
5. For overlapping or weak pages, pass unique material and an exact proposed disposition to [Review duplicate or weak pages](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=remove-duplicate-thin-pages#task-remove-duplicate-thin-pages). Redirect only when the reviewed replacement truly serves the old intent; no equivalent replacement may require a proper not-found response. Do not hide unresolved decisions behind an irrelevant nearest-hub redirect.
6. Apply only the authorized content and routing changes through their maintained sources, with current-source guards and retained media. Verify the real link in the normal rendered body and the destination’s actual response. A saved row or category reassignment is not evidence that a reader can reach the page.
7. Re-crawl the agreed scope and compare each original candidate with the new incoming paths. Report connected pages, deliberate exceptions, merges/removals and remaining failures separately. - [ ] Each accepted connection is a verified incoming path from a relevant live page.
- [ ] Exceptions and destructive decisions have explicit reasons and authority; no blanket redirect or false zero-orphan claim is used.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

The older SEO Tree article also uses “root” for the homepage; label that viewpoint if retained instead of inventing a second homepage or forcing incompatible labels.
3. Identify existing topic/method hubs and buying/service pages from their real purpose and the site’s navigation. The Money Tree can group branches into actual audience or offer limbs. Do not manufacture an ideal category structure or treat every topic hub as an executable task recipe.

# Remove duplicate thin pages

Keep your best page and the useful facts it holds. This guide checks weak or repeated pages and plans what to keep, join or remove. Start with the pages that seem to serve the same need and read what each one adds.

**The path:** Suspect URLs → Intent and evidence review → Keep or change proposal → Guarded release checks

**Start when:** The content inventory has identified possible duplicate intent or pages with little useful original value.

## Inputs

- [Inventory pages and their purpose](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page#task-step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page) and [Map actual content roles](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves#task-map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves) with current roles, links and possible overlap.
- Exact current source, media, search/referral data when available, business function and useful facts for every affected URL.
- The existing source/redirect owner, recovery copy and explicit authority for the exact consolidation, deletion or route change.

## Steps

1. Treat similar titles, low word counts and repeated phrases as review signals, not verdicts. Read each page’s actual promise, audience, method, proof and business function. A short contact page, service page and detailed how-to can all be useful; shared terms do not make them interchangeable.
2. Identify the owning intent and any genuinely equivalent URLs. List unique facts, examples, links, media, attribution, comments or conversion functions that a change must preserve. Review available search and referral evidence with its period and limits; missing measurement is unknown, not proof that a page has no value.
3. Choose keep, improve, merge, canonical-review or remove for each exact URL, with a reason and owner. A canonical hint can identify a preferred duplicate representation but does not itself delete content or guarantee the selected search URL. Avoid turning every overlapping story into a competing-hub problem.
4. For a merge, place the useful unique material into the true equivalent destination and review the new whole page. Preserve source ownership, relevant media and claims; do not copy unsupported assertions merely because they existed in the old draft. Verify that the replacement serves what old visitors expected.
5. Prepare a precise route map. Use a permanent redirect when content has moved to a relevant replacement; if removed content has no equivalent, an appropriate 404 or 410 may be correct. An unrelated closest-hub redirect can mislead readers and be treated as a soft error. Never create a redirect loop or chain as a shortcut.
6. Apply authorized source and routing changes in the agreed sequence with current-source guards and recovery evidence. Update controlled internal links to the final relevant targets and verify generated sitemap behavior through the maintained tool. A sitemap refresh or canonical tag does not guarantee Google has reprocessed the change.
7. Check the normal old and new URLs, actual content/media, statuses, canonical signals and important page functions. Re-crawl affected links and record what changed, what remains pending and the observation date. - [ ] Unique useful material, media, attribution and business function are preserved in the approved result.
- [ ] Every redirect has a relevant replacement, and old/new normal responses and links are checked.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

## Steps

Export all published content types in scope, including Posts and Pages where used, and reconcile them with sitemap and crawl. A crawl alone can miss unlinked URLs; list inaccessible or excluded source areas explicitly.
2. Keep one row per actual canonical content item with URL, source ID/type, title, publish/modified dates, current source revision, categories/tags where supported and page owner if known. Retain aliases and redirects in separate fields so normalization does not erase a real split or routing issue.
3. Add incoming and outgoing link counts with their extraction source and date. Distinguish rendered-body links from theme navigation and count unique sources consistently. State the reader’s actual situation and desired action, the real method or proof supplied, and who the page serves. For money pages, use the genuine offer and buying path; for a recipe, identify the task result rather than a generic traffic goal.
5. Assign the honest content role and map location. Use the current tree legend without inventing a separate homepage/root node. Task recipes, topic hubs, service pages, supporting stories and utility pages have different jobs even if they share keywords; their evidence and readiness states stay distinct.
6. Check grade-five context, why the reader should care, useful outcome and the body’s supporting mechanism. - [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

# Step 2: Fix categories and tags in WordPress

Help readers browse your posts in groups that make sense. This guide fixes mixed-up page groups and labels without breaking the site. Start with your page list and the groups the site already uses.

**The path:** Page roles + current terms → Term mapping → Approved assignments → Archive and API checks

**Start when:** Step 1 is accepted and the WordPress site’s categories or tags need a scoped cleanup.

## Inputs

- [Inventory pages and their purpose](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page#task-step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page) with actual post/page types, page roles, current term IDs and source owner.
- The live WordPress category/tag definitions, archive routes, theme/plugin dependencies and any taxonomy-enabled custom types.
- The approved term mapping and edit scope, preserved source copy and current site permalink rules.

## Steps

1. Read the current terms and supported content types from the actual WordPress source. Record term ID, name, slug, parent, count and archive URL. Default WordPress Posts support categories and tags; Pages need explicit registered support, so do not assume every page accepts the same fields.
2. Compare categories with real topic groups and reader navigation. A category can support a branch but is not automatically the canonical hub itself. Preserve valid site-specific roles and distinguish task-definitive pages from topic, comparison and historical content instead of assigning every important page the same label.
3. Prepare an old-to-new mapping with the exact affected content items. Reuse stable valid terms and IDs where possible. Use tags for useful cross-cutting attributes such as an actual stage or topic; do not invent a Content Factory stage for support work that spans several stages.
4. Review empty, one-off and similar terms for purpose and dependencies before proposing removal. Low count alone does not prove a term is useless. Check archive use, menus, inbound links, permalink settings and integrations; term deletion or slug changes may require a separately reviewed routing plan.
5. Apply accepted assignments through the supported editor or REST API when authorized. For the standard Posts API, categories and tags use term-ID arrays, and list filters use the documented plural parameters. Resolve real IDs; a guessed category-slug query is not evidence that an agent can retrieve the desired group.
6. Inspect the affected archive pages and representative content after the change. Check that visible labels, links, pagination and relevant grouping work, that useful hubs still lead correctly, and that unrelated categories or media were not overwritten by a partial update.

# Step 3: Identify money pages and orphan pages

## Steps

2. Flag pages with no detected incoming internal route using the inventory’s stated scope. Keep outgoing links, navigation links, body-link counts and assigned parent separate. # Step 4: Create links with proper anchor text and placement

Put useful next steps where readers need them. This guide adds clear links between pages that truly help each other. Start with the checked link plan and the current text of each page you will change.

**The path:** Accepted link rows → Fresh source check → Contextual edit → Saved and public readback

**Start when:** Step 3 has supplied accepted source-to-target rows and the exact content edits are authorized.

## Inputs

- Fresh source/body for each page, maintained builder/generator rail, existing media and the expected base revision.
- [Choose the right entity destination](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=follow-entity-linking-decision-tree#task-follow-entity-linking-decision-tree) and the baseline request for [Measure the accepted change set](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-6-measure-and-iterate-with-maa#task-step-6-measure-and-iterate-with-maa) before release, where measurement is planned.

## Steps

1. Open each plan row and fetch the current maintained source before editing. Compare it with the reviewed base and preserve concurrent work. Identify whether a builder, shortcode, generator or ordinary body owns the text; do not replace serialized layout or generated content with a blind full-body write.
2. Read both source and target in context and confirm the planned reader benefit still holds. If the target has changed, redirects to a different subject or does not deliver the proposed promise, hold or revise the row with its owner. A once-approved URL is not a permanent relevance guarantee.
3. Choose concise anchor text that honestly predicts the destination. Prefer three to six descriptive words when natural, or use the actual entity name. Avoid padding, generic “click here,” keyword stuffing and forced phrasing changes that make repeated references less clear.
4. Place the link in the relevant body sentence with enough context to explain why it helps. Useful existing navigation and footers may remain; this task is not a site-wide ban on those links. Add no hidden links or unrelated collections merely to increase the total.
5. Apply [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/) to explanations while preserving direct primary evidence and actual account/download actions. Connect stories to their owning methods or offers and add useful cross-links as planned. Keep the source’s factual meaning, relevant proof, IDs and media unchanged outside the exact intended edit.
6. If a suggestion tool proposes additional links, treat them as candidates requiring the same purpose and identity review. Do not accept a batch solely from a keyword score. Log rejected and held rows so the accepted scope does not silently expand during implementation.
7. Save through the supported authorized rail and read back the exact edited field and ordinary rendered page. Follow the real link and check its final target and surrounding sentence. # Step 5: QA links against Google guidelines

Check that each new link helps readers reach the right page. This guide tests the words, the page they open and the reason to click. Start with the exact list of links that changed and their live pages.

**The path:** Exact changed links → Meaning and destination checks → Repairs or held rows → Accepted log

**Start when:** Step 4 has saved or released a defined set of links and supplied the actual change log.

## Inputs

- [Place the accepted links](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-4-create-links-with-proper-anchor-text-and-placement#task-step-4-create-links-with-proper-anchor-text-and-placement) log with source/target, anchor, surrounding text, exact revision and save/public state.
- The accepted [Goals, Content, Targeting: the result, source material and people served](https://blitzmetrics.com/gct-business-strategy/) and current owning target pages, plus normal public access to the changed source pages.
- The maintained [internal-linking method](https://blitzmetrics.com/internal-linking/) and current Google primary link guidance.

## Steps

1. Start from the exact changed-link log and read each link in its actual normal page context. Compare it with the saved source, not just a preview or cached screenshot. A stale public copy or inaccessible page is a specific verification gap; do not approve it because the CMS raw text is correct.
2. Check the anchor’s promise against the destination. It should be concise, descriptive and natural; the house three-to-six-word preference is not a Google word-count rule. A real two-word name can be correct, and repeating an accurate name is not automatically keyword stuffing.
3. Check that the surrounding sentence gives a useful reason to follow the link and remains factually true. Confirm the named person, company, method or offer matches. Owned explanatory links must not replace a necessary primary citation, sign-in or download destination with a general guide.
4. Inspect placement and link behavior. Ordinary crawlable links use real anchors with destinations, and readers must be able to see and use them. Contextual body links are this change set’s purpose; useful menu/footer navigation is not inherently manipulative. Hold hidden, misleading or unrelated link schemes.
5. Review volume by reader usefulness rather than a fixed links-per-word ratio. Remove redundant or forced additions where they add no value. Google states no ideal link count; a page with many relevant sources and a short page with few links need different judgments.
6. Follow each changed destination and record actual responses and redirect meaning. Correct a stale internal alias when the verified final target serves the same purpose; do not rewrite an intentional external evidence link blindly. Handle removed content with a relevant replacement or the proper reviewed removal behavior, never an arbitrary redirect.
7. Repair in-scope defects through the same maintained source rail and repeat only the affected checks. Save accepted, failed and held rows with exact evidence and owners, plus any wider issues discovered outside this scope. Pass the verified change set to measurement without declaring full-site compliance from a limited link review.

## Definition of done (QA checklist)

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] Each accepted changed link has an accurate anchor, useful context, correct identity and actual destination check.
- [ ] The review distinguishes Google guidance from house preferences and finds no hidden or irrelevant link scheme in the changed set.
- [ ] Source/public mismatches, failed links and out-of-scope defects retain their real states and owners.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

## Example(s)

**Fictional teaching example. This is not a client result or proof of a completed run.**

A fictional review checks eight new links. Seven point to the intended pages. The eighth uses a service name but now redirects to a general home page, so it is held until the owner confirms a relevant destination. # Step 6: Measure and iterate with MAA

2. Collect comparable page/query search measures such as clicks, impressions and average position from the actual connected source. Collect relevant sessions or observed inquiries only when those systems are accessible and their definitions are known. Keep disconnected, filtered or delayed data unknown rather than zero.
3. Use consistent properties, periods, filters and URL handling for before/after comparisons. Keep search measures, sessions, link clicks and business outcomes separate; one is not a substitute for another. 4. Check whether the intended paths are still live and useful, especially former orphans and important offer links. A new crawl can establish incoming connections; it does not prove search indexing or a sale. Indexing observations and rank measures require their own source and date.
5. Write the analysis in terms the evidence supports. A rise after the edits is an observed association, not proof that one anchor caused it. Explain plausible competing causes and what further observation would distinguish them. Do not claim to identify which individual link “did the work” from a page-level traffic total.
6. Choose a bounded next action tied to the finding: repair a broken relevant path, improve a weak source, inspect a missing data source, retain a useful link or wait for adequate data. Do not change anchors or remove helpful links simply because a short window shows no traffic gain.

# Use proper anchor text (3–6 words, descriptive)

Help readers know where a link will take them. This guide replaces vague link words with clear names and useful phrases. Start with the links you plan to change and read each page they open.

**The path:** Anchor and context list → Destination promise check → Natural wording → Rendered link review

**Start when:** A draft or bounded existing-page audit contains vague, misleading or needlessly padded link text.

## Inputs

- The current source pages and a bounded anchor report, with exact href, surrounding sentence and source revision.
- The real destination content and [Goals, Content, Targeting: the result, source material and people served](https://blitzmetrics.com/gct-business-strategy/), plus [Choose the right entity destination](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=follow-entity-linking-decision-tree#task-follow-entity-linking-decision-tree) for identity and owned-explanation routes.
- The supported content source/builder, edit authority and relevant existing media/IDs to preserve.

## Steps

1. List the actual links in scope and read their surrounding copy. Flag vague words such as “click here,” a bare URL in ordinary explanatory prose, misleading names or excessive keyword repetition. Keep functional citations, legal identifiers and platform controls in their proper context instead of blindly replacing every URL string.
2. Read each destination and state what the reader gets there. Check that its person, company, topic or action matches the link’s promise. A link that opens a different page needs a destination decision before better wording can make it useful.
3. Write a concise descriptive phrase, usually three to six words when natural. Use the actual entity name where it is clearer, even if shorter. This is a house writing preference, not a Google minimum or maximum, and padding “Dennis Yu” into a longer phrase can make the reference less accurate.
4. Place the wording in a sentence that explains why the next page helps. Keep it natural for the author and reader. Reuse a correct name consistently where appropriate; do not force synonyms merely to make anchors look varied, and do not overload a phrase with search terms.
5. Preserve the difference between an owned explanation, a primary evidence citation and a necessary account or download action. Label the exact purpose and use its appropriate destination. A general method link cannot fulfill a button’s promise to open the real sign-in page.
6. Apply the narrow wording edit through the maintained source and inspect the result. Ensure that the clickable span includes the intended words, punctuation remains correct, and surrounding text, media and identifiers are unchanged. Check keyboard use and responsive layout for any affected link or button.
7. After authorized release, open the normal page and follow the edited link. Save the exact before/after anchor, href, revision and public evidence. Report resolved, held and intentionally retained cases within the stated scope; do not claim a whole-site cleanup from a sample or a failed fetch.

# Publish an SEO Tree site directory

**The path:** Checked hierarchy → Clickable map + text list → Source and visual checks → Public directory

**Start when:** The site’s checked hierarchy is ready for a public directory on its own domain.

## Inputs

- [Map actual content roles](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves#task-map-content-hierarchically-root-trunk-branches-leaves) with actual URL roles, entity home, topic/offer branches and supporting pages.
- Current source/builder, any existing directory URL, approved publishing scope and public-safe identity evidence.
- The [SEO Tree, the map that links a site’s proof to its main topics and offers](https://blitzmetrics.com/seo-tree-site-directory/) method, current [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/) and real node/label data rather than decorative example leaves.

## Steps

1. Inspect the existing site directory and the source that owns it. Improve the current canonical route where it already serves this job. Choose a new directory path only when needed and agreed; do not rename a live method article or change the site’s routing just to force a preferred slug.
2. Use the verified entity home as trunk, actual major topics and offers as branches, and relevant existing content as leaves. Identify off-site roots from genuine identity or proof sources. An appearance, a profile and praise are distinct evidence types; the map must not imply endorsements that those sources do not contain.
3. Check each selected branch against the current site’s own navigation and content. Link its actual owning URL and describe what a visitor can learn or do there. Keep task recipes separate from topic hubs and historical stories. Missing or duplicate owners become explicit repair items before they are presented as resolved.
4. Build a useful clickable visual and matching visible text outline from the same data. Use clear groups, labels and real anchors that work with a keyboard. Show the actual scoped breadth; if the lead view is simplified, label its coverage and give a direct path to the complete directory.
5. Write a short grade-five opening that explains why this specific map helps the reader and how to use it. Put meaningful map content in the first desktop and mobile screen, followed by concise role explanations and real links. Preserve authentic relevant media and avoid a full-screen decorative title card.
6. Check every node’s destination, the text/visual agreement, public-safe source facts and the rendered page. Unknown destinations stay held or clearly labeled. Search-friendly markup can clarify visible facts but does not guarantee indexing, rankings or a search feature. Keep client metrics and private evidence out of public hidden data as well as visible copy.

# Build a Money Tree site diagram

See which parts of your site help people find what you sell. This guide draws a tree from the links your pages really have. Start with your full page list and the offers people can buy.

**The path:** Published URLs + offer list → Measured body links → Tree and text view → Owned fixes

**Start when:** An eligible managed site needs its existing monthly tree rebuild or a specifically authorized structure audit.

## Inputs

- [Inventory pages and their purpose](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page#task-step-1-inventory-content-and-establish-gct-per-page) with published posts, pages, content types, current body output, date and crawl coverage.
- The actual home, navigation, services and method pages; canonical targets, previous tree and its count definition.
- The maintained Money Tree renderer/source contract and authorized site scope; private measurements only from connected, verified sources.

## Steps

1. Read the current [Money Tree, a site map whose branch sizes show measured supporting links](https://blitzmetrics.com/money-tree/) procedure and existing renderer contract. Confirm the site is eligible and its owner, publication rail, previous run and scope. Use the real home/domain as trunk, existing audience or offer groups as limbs, real method or buying pages as branches, and off-site identity proof as roots.
2. Fetch all published URLs from the supported source and reconcile with the crawl. Include both WordPress Posts and Pages where present. Use rendered article bodies to expand builder or shortcode links, while retaining the source revision and extraction boundaries; list unreadable or missing pages explicitly.
3. Extract actual internal body links and build an inbound index. Count each published post once per branch even if it links there several times. Keep page-to-page links separate and exclude theme navigation from this leaf count. Normalize only documented equivalent URL forms; do not erase meaningful query parameters blindly.
4. Identify the branches from the site’s current navigation, services and topic owners. Follow and record redirects. Group confirmed aliases with a union of distinct source posts, naming the old paths and duplicates as findings. Similar titles alone do not prove two live offers are the same branch.
5. Generate the dated clickable diagram, matching linked text outline and truthful structured metadata from that same checked data. Branch weight follows the source-defined count; bare branches remain bare. Label a simplified opening view and link directly to the full tree so no omitted branch disappears from the review.
6. Check all in-scope offers are represented, nodes resolve or are clearly held, and the three representations agree. Reproduce counts from the saved snapshot rather than expecting a changing live site to freeze. Review useful labels and coverage at desktop and mobile sizes; decoration must not invent supporting leaves.
7. Prepare the public structural view and authenticated private measurement view separately. Keep client leads, revenue and priorities out of public HTML, hidden data, metadata and alt text. When release is authorized, verify the normal URL against the exact saved source and retain rollback evidence.
8. Record bare branches, split destinations, redirects, broken targets and relevant proof gaps with exact URLs, counts and owners. Use verified comparable revenue only for a revenue ranking; disconnected data remains unknown. Hand the accepted tree and deltas to the existing review owner without creating another schedule.

run identity. The actual home/domain is the trunk, buying/service destinations
are branches, and relevant published supporting articles/videos are leaves.
Link real nodes to their canonical destinations and retain unknown branches.
The tree is evidence of site structure; it must never imply unmeasured results.

Each buying page has meaningful relevant proof above the fold, evidence beside
material outcome claims, and relevant proof near its primary buying action.
Use the full tree or its useful branch where it explains the offer, alongside
real project scenes, attributable results and source videos. Give supporting
leaves a relevant buying destination and a practical how-to link when useful.
Keep public wording confident and specific: state the sourced moment once;
remove repeated caveats, internal review scores and unsupported claims.

Public trees contain public structure and content counts only. Private sessions,
leads, bookings, conversion rates, revenue, finances and priorities stay behind
authenticated client access, including alt text, metadata, hidden DOM and JSON-LD.
NOT_CONNECTED is not zero. Preserve the existing roster, site authorization,
CMS/deployment/rollback and public/private gates; a schedule or current recipe
is not a release receipt. Reconcile `monthly-client-money-tree-maa` before adding
any clock. Check priority buying pages and named relationships weekly; rebuild
other eligible site trees monthly through their existing owning function.

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] Public diagram, text and metadata agree; private values are absent from every public representation.
- [ ] Each priority finding has a specific next task and owner; structural counts are not claimed as measured sales.
- [ ] Every branch in the service/navigation scope is represented
- [ ] Counts are reproducible and links resolve or are flagged
- [ ] Diagram, outline and schema agree
- [ ] A simplified opening map states its selection and coverage and leads directly to the complete tree; meaningful groups preserve the scoped tree's actual breadth without invented nodes or decorative leaves

# Close endorsement links for an ended relationship

Keep your site clear about who you work with now. This guide checks old links when a work relationship ends, while keeping true history. Start with the agreed change and the pages your team can edit.

**The path:** Confirmed relationship change → Controlled-link inventory → Narrow edits → Public closeout check

**Start when:** The relationship owner has confirmed a specific ended relationship and the public association that must change.

## Inputs

- A dated source confirming the relationship’s end, the exact entities involved, affected roles and decision owner.
- The relevant controlled sites, public profiles and draft records, with current edit rights and release authority.
- Existing account/access ownership, historical facts to preserve and the [relationship closeout method](https://blitzmetrics.com/when-trust-ends-the-link-ends/).

## Steps

1. Confirm the actual event and scope with the owning record. Distinguish an ended agency relationship from a former employee role, an expired offer or an unsupported allegation. If the owner’s decision is missing, stage the inventory and leave the public change pending.
2. Inventory affected links and association claims only on surfaces the team controls. Save the exact URL, surrounding sentence, destination, role and current source. Use explicit searches and known site maps; an incomplete search is a bounded inventory, not proof that all web references were found.
3. Classify each item as current endorsement, active role, factual historical record, primary evidence or unrelated identity reference. The closeout removes misleading current association while retaining true history. An old event appearance or dated quote does not become false simply because the working relationship ended.
4. Prepare the smallest appropriate edit for each confirmed current endorsement. Remove a hyperlink, qualify the former role or revise its surrounding sentence as warranted. Never retarget the other party’s name to your own site and leave a misleading anchor; a new destination requires a truthful label and relevant purpose.
5. Keep account and infrastructure ownership separate. Remove only an explicitly authorized obsolete role or access grant after checking the correct account and recovery dependency. Do not delete the other party’s site, transfer their domain, lock them out or change unrelated administrators as a side effect.
6. Use the supported content rail for authorized edits, preserving current source, media and unrelated fields. Check the normal anonymous page and link behavior after save. Public caches or inaccessible profiles remain specific verification gaps; a successful save response alone does not prove the public association changed.
7. Save before/after evidence, unchanged history, inaccessible surfaces and each remaining owner. Any notice to the other party needs its own send authority. Complete the scoped closeout when its actual checks pass, without claiming control over copies or accounts outside the agreed boundary.

# Add consistent headshots and bios across profiles

# Build personal brand website

## Steps

1. Inspect any existing site, source owner, pages, mail setup and current links before planning changes. Improve the maintained site in place when possible. Separate the content build from domain registration, DNS changes, hosting charges and public launch authority.
2. Build the first screen around who the person is, what they do and useful proof for the intended reader. Use two or three plain sentences at grade five or below, a real photo or evidence-backed diagram, and one clear next step. Preserve the person’s authentic voice.
3. Build About, work/method, evidence and contact sections from verified source material. Explain each named result with its scope and source. Keep first person for the person’s own account, attributed quotes for others, and remove empty promises rather than inventing testimonials.
4. Use real photos and relevant usable video when available, with captions and context. Keep a missing video as an asset gap. Check embeds silently, muted at zero volume; a working embed is not proof that an unheard audio track is intelligible.
5. Add useful routes to the person’s verified profiles and related work. Apply [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/) and the [SEO Tree, the map from proof pages to main topics and offers](https://blitzmetrics.com/seo-tree/). Prepare the structured identity markup through its dedicated task so a theme, plugin and custom block do not create competing Person identities.

Check HTTPS, indexing controls and the actual measurement plan before launch; a performance score is a measurement, not a universal three-second guarantee.

# Classify and offer Knowledge Panel

Choose the right next step for your name on Google. This guide checks what is there before your team offers panel work. Start with a fresh search and the current terms your business has approved.

**The path:** Live search + proof → Claim / Build / Contested → Current terms → Offer draft

**Start when:** An accepted prospective engagement needs an evidence-based panel-work recommendation and a matching draft offer.

## Inputs

- The person’s accepted public name, role, home site and existing identity evidence.
- Current search access, the approved service terms and qualification rules, and the actual commercial decision owner.
- [Current owned package page](https://localservicespotlight.com/knowledge-panel-package/) and [Google’s account of how panels work](https://support.google.com/knowledgepanel/answer/9163198?hl=en); reconcile any conflict with the accepted engagement before quoting.

## Steps

# Create social content from video clips

Make short clips from your real videos. This guide turns a real source into short clips and clear post drafts. Start with the best complete answer and the people it should help.

**The path:** Checked source → Complete short clip → Platform post draft → Release and results

**Start when:** A usable video source needs short social versions for selected channels.

## Inputs

- [Record real customer answers](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=record-one-minute-videos-answering-customer-questions#task-record-one-minute-videos-answering-customer-questions) or another permitted source with speaker, date, transcript and exact file.
- The agreed channels, audience, main point, destination and source rights.
- Actual editing tool, caption process, current platform limits and release owner.

## Steps

1. Read the source and pick a complete idea that works without misleading cuts. Use the source’s roughly 15–60 second range as an editing target when it suits the story and placement. Preserve necessary context; split or lengthen a point that cannot be honestly shortened.
2. Cut from the real file and keep speaker, facts and sequence accurate. Do not manufacture a quote from unrelated fragments. Retain the source timestamp range and transcript so another reviewer can compare the clip with the original.
3. Add accurate captions, checking names and numbers manually against the source. Preview the face, key action, text and caption safe areas at the intended size. Review media silently with mute and volume zero; use transcript or measurements for audio checks if listening is not authorized.
4. Write each post for its actual audience and channel. Lead with the useful point, use a truthful hook and explain unfamiliar terms. A channel may need a different length or title, but do not rewrite merely to force different wording where the same message fits.
5. Choose the relevant owned destination using [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/). Use a clickable post link where supported or the correct profile route where it is not. Credit or tag verified participants only when relevant and consistent with the release scope.
6. Prepare the complete media, copy and destination for review. Publish only on the channels authorized, using their supported controls. Open each actual public post after release and check the source, captions, crop and route; record unavailable or pending surfaces honestly.
7. Save the exact asset/post IDs and later date-bounded metrics in the existing content record. Keep planned, exported, posted and measured states separate. Pass comparable results to the creative-selection task rather than assuming a posted clip is a winner.

## Definition of done (QA checklist)

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] Only observed posts are labeled live and their later metrics retain source and period.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

## Example(s)

**Fictional teaching example. This is not a client result or proof of a completed run.**

# Establish entity identity

# Generate backlinks and entity mentions

Help readers find your work from places they already use. This guide helps you earn links by doing useful work. Start with the links you have and the ones your readers need.

**The path:** Existing mentions → Useful target list → Real contribution → Checked credit

**Start when:** The site has useful proof and the team needs a bounded plan to earn or recover relevant editorial credits.

## Inputs

- The current backlink and mention inventory, home URL and approved identity facts.
- Actual audience needs, relevant work to cite and a list of suitable publications, shows, events or associations.
- Outreach owner and scope, source/reuse rights, and the existing proof record.

## Steps

1. Record the current baseline and its coverage: known source URLs, referring domains, mention text, date and destination. A tool export may be incomplete; unavailable or unindexed sources are not automatically absent from the web.
2. Prioritize destinations by audience fit, editorial relevance and actual relationships. Prefer a missing credit for real work, a useful expert contribution or a relevant member listing over a generic domain-authority target. Do not claim to know which source Google trusts most.
3. Use the relevant podcast, speaking, press or collaboration recipe to prepare a specific contribution. Supply facts, original experience and source proof. An exchange intended chiefly to manipulate rankings is not the editorial relationship this task teaches.
4. Prepare a concise credit or correction request to the actual source owner when it would help the reader. Link the accepted name to the verified home where editorially suitable. Requesting a link does not guarantee the host will add it, and no send is implied without authority.

# Get featured on podcasts

Share your useful work with people who listen to the right shows. This guide helps you plan a guest pitch and follow the episode through release. Start with one show and a topic its listeners need.

**The path:** Audience fit → Specific pitch → Agreed recording → Released episode and reuse

**Start when:** The person has real expertise and a suitable show may benefit from a guest conversation.

## Inputs

- A verified show list, actual recent episodes and audience fit.

- Outreach authority, guest availability, recording/use consent and the show’s actual submission route.

## Steps

1. Read or inspect a real recent episode and the show’s guest process. Prioritize audience fit and useful subject matter, not just a promise of backlinks. Record the host, source, topic opportunity and any published submission requirements.
2. Prepare a compact pitch kit with current bio, photo, a few relevant talk ideas and verified source links. Explain what listeners will learn. Avoid unsupported performance numbers, borrowed credentials or an assumption that a famous previous guest endorses the new one.
3. Draft a personal pitch tied to the actual show and one clear topic. Send only with the existing authority and retain the exact thread. Track drafted, sent, replied, accepted and booked states separately; no-reply remains no-reply.

Help the right readers learn from your real work. This guide turns a useful fact or story into a clear press pitch. Start with a source you can prove and a writer who covers that topic.

**The path:** Real story + proof → Relevant writer → Specific pitch → Checked coverage

**Start when:** The person has a verifiable story or expert contribution suitable for a publication.

## Inputs

- A source-backed story, useful data or expert response, with permission to share the material.
- A current press kit, accepted name and home site, and a verified publication/writer list.
- Submission rules, deadline and outreach owner; this task’s dedicated canonical article remains unmapped.

## Steps

1. Choose outlets and writers whose actual recent work covers the topic. Read the editorial focus and submission rules. A prestigious name alone does not make the story relevant, and a purchased placement is not independent earned coverage.
2. Build the pitch around a true new fact, useful lesson or timely perspective. Verify numbers, dates, qualifications and client permission. State what the source proves and what remains uncertain; do not create news by inventing a milestone.
3. Prepare a concise response or pitch with the reader value, specific angle, supporting sources and a relevant bio. Keep quotes attributable and in the person’s voice. Use [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/) for plain context and proof, without turning the message into a company sales page.
4. Send through the writer’s real accepted channel only under existing authority. Track the exact message, recipient, deadline and reply. If a journalist asks a follow-up, verify the new facts before preparing an answer; speed does not substitute for accuracy.
5. Coordinate any interview or source material with the actual editorial terms, attribution and use rights. Paid promotion is a separate optional task; do not assume an ad can or should target an individual journalist before a pitch.
6. When coverage is reported, inspect the published source for the correct identity, exact quoted meaning, disclosure and link. Prepare a factual correction if needed and keep requested versus accepted changes distinct. A pitch or interview does not establish publication.
7. Add the verified source to the proof inventory with date, independence, permission and exact supported claim. Keep the missing canonical task article as a visible mapping gap; use the current personal-brand method hub for context without calling it this task’s finished recipe.

## Definition of done (QA checklist)

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] The story and pitch are useful, supported and addressed to a relevant actual outlet.
- [ ] Every claimed published item is checked; pending or declined pitches remain honest.
- [ ] Proof, permission and attribution are recorded, and the dedicated article gap remains visible.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

**Fictional teaching example. This is not a client result or proof of a completed run.**

A fictional shop owner has measured a seasonal rise in one repair type. The team checks the date range and sample, then drafts a local trade story. # Link all content back to personal brand site

Help readers reach the right next page from your work. This guide checks links in posts, profiles and guest features. Start with your live content list and the site that should be your public home.

**The path:** Asset list → Right destination → Owned edits or host request → Checked path

**Start when:** A bounded set of published assets needs its identity and topic links checked.

## Inputs

- The current content inventory with exact URLs, platform and edit owner.
- Verified person/company sites and relevant topic/offer pages; [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/) and the [SEO Tree, the map from proof pages to main topics and offers](https://blitzmetrics.com/seo-tree/).
- Actual edit/send authority and the previous link audit, if one exists.

## Steps

1. Set the scope from the existing inventory and add newly discovered assets there. Record URL, publisher, article purpose, current destination and edit owner. A known list is a bounded audit scope, not proof that every asset on the web has been found.
2. Choose the useful destination for each first mention. The person’s name points to their verified home, a company to its own site, and a method to its maintained guide. A source citation or required tool action keeps its direct source rather than being replaced with an irrelevant internal page.
3. Use meaningful anchor text that identifies the person or destination naturally. The house three-to-six-word preference is a guide, not permission to pad a two-word person’s name or change the sentence’s meaning. Do not repeatedly link the same entity in one piece.
4. On the owned site, check a real path from each supporting page to its topic and relevant offer under the SEO Tree. Add a useful parent link and related proof where appropriate. Avoid forcing every article directly to the homepage when a more specific branch serves the reader.
5. On social pages, use the supported website field or relevant post link. If a channel makes links non-clickable, record the actual profile or other supported path and test it. Do not claim every post contains a clickable link when the platform does not provide one.
6. For a third-party feature, prepare a specific factual credit/link request to its actual editor under send authority. Keep pending, declined and accepted outcomes separate. The host controls its editorial links; a refused link does not erase a real mention.
7. After authorized changes, follow each repaired path from the normal public asset to the intended page. Save exact URLs, source revision, results and remaining owner actions. Review newly released or changed content through this same bounded method; recurring timing needs an actual owner.

## Definition of done (QA checklist)

Quality assurance (QA) means checking the actual result against its agreed requirements. Follow the [Article Guidelines](https://localservicespotlight.com/article-guidelines/).

- [ ] Each in-scope asset has a checked useful path or a specific supported limitation and next owner.
- [ ] Identity links, topic hierarchy and primary citations retain their correct purposes.
- [ ] Repaired links are publicly read back; outside requests are not counted as accepted edits.
- [ ] The exact output, source revision, reviewer evidence and remaining owner action are saved.
- [ ] For any reader-facing output, the short grade-five opening states the reader’s useful outcome and supporting method or proof. The body delivers that promise; a useful authentic visual appears in the first screen. Retain exact text and quoted reviewer evidence.

## Example(s)

**Fictional teaching example. This is not a client result or proof of a completed run.**

A fictional coach’s interview links to an old home page. Her own recap can be changed, so it receives the correct topic link and her current home. The host’s show notes need an editor request. # Record one-minute videos answering customer questions

## Steps

3. Prepare a brief prompt and source reminders instead of a fabricated first-person script. # Register personal name domain

# Repurpose videos into blog posts via Content Factory

Make a clear page from a real video. This guide keeps your real voice and proof while making the lesson clear. Start with one checked recording and the reader it should help.

**The path:** Real recording → Checked transcript → Useful article → Reviewed release

**Start when:** A permitted usable recording needs a source-backed article on the person’s maintained site.

## Steps

Read any existing article on the topic before drafting; improve the maintained owner or create the appropriate supporting page under the [SEO Tree, the map from proof pages to main topics and offers](https://blitzmetrics.com/seo-tree/) rather than duplicate a competing topic hub.
2. Transcribe with the tool actually available, then compare names, numbers and load-bearing statements with the source. Keep exact timestamps for useful quotes and corrections. A transcript is evidence to check, not permission to invent a more impressive story.
3. Define [Goals, Content, Targeting: the result, source material and people served](https://blitzmetrics.com/gct-business-strategy/) from the actual material and assignment. Draft the short opening at grade five or below, explaining the reader’s situation, useful outcome and supporting method. 4. Write a clear article with title under 60 characters, concise meta description under 160, useful headings and short active paragraphs. Preserve the person’s authentic first-person account and named credited quotes. Include relevant credibility proof; do not rewrite a lived example into generic advice or a claim the speaker never made.
5. Place meaningful real media or a source-backed diagram with the short opening and embed the source video where permitted and useful. Check captions, source identity and responsive layout silently with volume zero. Do not substitute an empty featured-image box for actual first-screen evidence.

Use [entity linking, choosing the right home for a named person or topic](https://blitzmetrics.com/entity-linking/) for correct person, company and method destinations; retain primary proof links where they support a claim. 8. Save transcript/source links, exact draft or public revision, review results and remaining actions in the existing content record. Hand real sources and accepted excerpts to the clip task; writing an article does not mean its social derivatives or promotion have run.

# Run Thank You Machine for every interaction

2. Choose the appropriate route for the person and situation. Some thanks belong in a private note; others may become public content with the right permission. An interaction does not automatically consent to a public story, tag, testimonial or ad.

Consider [Dollar a Day, small paid tests of proven content](https://blitzmetrics.com/dollar-a-day/) only for an appropriate public asset with useful organic evidence, use rights, tracking and a separately approved test budget. Gratitude does not require paid amplification, and a nominal daily budget is not a guarantee of outcome or zero risk.

# Keep speaker bureau profile bookable

Give event hosts the facts they need to book your talk. This guide keeps your speaker page and booking profile in line with one approved kit. Start with your current talks, fees and real proof.

# Secure guest appearances and speaking engagements

Find a stage where your work can help the room. This guide prepares a clear talk pitch and tracks what happens next. Start with the right event and a real lesson its guests can use.

**The path:** Audience fit → Specific talk pitch → Confirmed event → Delivered talk and proof

**Start when:** The speaker has a checked kit and a suitable event may benefit from a proposed talk or guest session.

## Inputs

- [Keep the speaker kit ready](https://local-service-spotlight.github.io/task-library/?task=keep-speaker-bureau-profile-bookable#task-keep-speaker-bureau-profile-bookable) with approved bio, talks, public fee terms and relevant real footage.
- Verified event list, audience needs, submission process and actual organizer route.
- Speaker availability, outreach authority, commercial decision owner and recording/use permissions.

## Steps

1. Inspect the event’s current audience, program and speaker-submission rules. Rank opportunities by the lesson the speaker can contribute and the people it serves. An event with a speaker page is useful evidence, but a listing or warm introduction does not guarantee a booking.
2. Adapt one real approved talk to that audience using the kit. State the problem, practical takeaways, format and relevant source proof. Do not invent a new credential, imply a prior event booked this talk without evidence or use generic fame as its only value.
3. Draft the precise organizer proposal and send only under existing authority. Track the original thread and real response. If fees, travel, rights or scope differ from the kit, prepare the exact terms for the authorized decision owner rather than accepting them implicitly.
4. After acceptance, confirm date, timezone, location or virtual platform, format, audience, fee terms and required assets. Save the actual confirmation. A tentative hold is not a public announced appearance or a delivered talk.
5. Check any permitted speaker page for correct identity, title, photo and useful home/booking link. Arrange real recording and photography rights with the organizer. A promise of footage is a dependency until the file is delivered and readable.
6. After the session, record what actually occurred and acquire the permitted source files. Hand off recording, photos, date, event context and use rights to the content team. Preserve a cancellation, missing footage or changed program honestly.
7. Prepare a useful recap, selected clips and specific acknowledgment through their own authorized release steps. Add the real appearance to the evidence record; a delivered talk is not automatically praise or proof of a wider partnership.

# Set up professional social profiles

Help people find the real you on the sites they use. This guide checks your work profiles and connects them to your own site. Start with the accounts you already control before you make new ones.

**The path:** Existing accounts → Right identity and ownership → Approved profile setup → Verified URL list

## Steps

1. Inventory current profiles, handles and account owners before creating anything. Separate wrong-person matches, abandoned accounts and potential duplicates. A duplicate-looking result needs an ownership check; it is not permission to delete an account or assume a claim right.

# Verify Google Business Profile

Help people find your local firm. Use this guide to check if your firm can have a profile on Google. Start with the way you serve your clients.

**The path:** Eligibility → Existing listing → Owner verification → Accurate public business facts

**Start when:** A qualifying business or eligible individual practitioner needs its Google Business Profile checked or verified.

## Inputs

- Business-owner authorization and Google account access, existing listing if any, and supporting business evidence.
- Current [Google’s business eligibility rules](https://support.google.com/business/answer/13763036?hl=en) and [representation rules](https://support.google.com/business/answer/3038177?hl=en).

## Steps

1. Check eligibility before opening a listing. Google generally requires in-person customer contact during stated hours; online-only personal brands do not qualify simply by having a website. Assess any practitioner under the actual public-facing and contact rules, not just the owner’s title.
2. Search for the existing business and distinguish it from the person’s Knowledge Panel. Confirm the right location, business and current ownership. Use the supported ownership-request path if another account manages it; do not create a duplicate to bypass the actual owner.
3. Use the real-world business name and accurate customer-facing contact details. Point the listing to the authoritative website for that business, not automatically the owner’s personal home. Apply the current address/service-area rules and hide a non-customer-facing address when required.
4. Follow the verification method Google actually offers in [its business verification flow](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7107242?hl=en). The business owner supplies required evidence or completes human identity steps. A postcard, phone, email or video option is not guaranteed for every account.
5. Keep owner control with the real business owner and use the minimum permitted helper role. Record account role and verification state privately. Do not use a public-looking badge or a helper’s recollection as proof of completed verification; inspect the actual managed profile state.
6. Prepare accurate categories, hours, description, service information and real photos under the listing’s actual rules. Do not add keywords to the business name, fake locations or unverifiable claims to make the listing look complete.
7. After authorized save, verify both the managed verification state and the normal public listing’s identity and facts. Pending verification stays pending.
